_comment: Expected repository settings. settings-audit.yml compares the live repository with this file daily. Role id 2 = maintain, 5 = admin. Every bypass actor is compared with its bypass_mode (`always` or `pull_request`): a missing actor, an extra actor and another mode are drift. The default-branch ruleset lets the admin role bypass in mode `pull_request` only: an admin can merge a pull request despite unmet rules (the policy check and the approval included), but cannot push to the default branch directly; the rule still requires a pull request for every change. The owner, the sole maintainer and code owner, cannot approve their own change, and accepts that single-maintainer changes to protected paths are approved by the owner. The tag and branch-creation rulesets list both roles in mode `always`, because the owner of a personal-account repository is an admin and a ruleset that only lets Maintain bypass would lock the owner out of tags. The pull_request object is the COMPLETE parameter object of that rule and required_status_checks_parameters is the complete parameter object of the status check rule without its list of checks: a parameter the live rule has that is not listed here, or another value, is drift. The four repo merge-method settings are returned by the API only to a caller with push access: a missing or null live value for them is not drift (the audit token is read-only), a returned value that differs is. The approvals are counted by the policy check (CODEOWNERS and a fresh approval of the exact head), so native required reviews stay off: they would stop the automatic merge of a pull request that needs no human. For the same reason `require_last_push_approval` is false: with a required approving review count of 0 it can make GitHub refuse the App's merge of an auto pull request; the policy check itself requires a fresh approval of the exact head, and `dismiss_stale_reviews_on_push` stays true. merge_commits.exempt_through: commits up to and including this commit were pushed directly to the default branch before the rulesets were applied and are exempt from the pull-request requirement of the commit check; every commit after it is checked. A value that is not a 40-digit lowercase hexadecimal sha fails the audit.
